Done. intervals.py rewritten and verified.

Implementation:
- Validates every pair first: non-int bounds or wrong length -> TypeError; start > end -> ValueError (all pairs checked before any merging).
- Sorts by (start, end), merges when next.start <= current.end (overlap or endpoint touch), returns a new list of tuples; input is never mutated (input rows are only read, results built fresh).
- Duplicate rows collapse into one merged interval (duplicates overlap, so merging handles them).

Verification: public_test.py prints "public tests passed", plus extra checks covering touching, gaps, containment, unordered input, duplicates, non-mutation, empty input, and all error cases — "all extra checks passed".

Note on interpretation: "touch" is treated as endpoint equality (e.g. (1,2)+(2,3) -> (1,3)); integer-adjacent intervals with a gap like (1,1)+(2,2) are left separate, consistent with the public test's (1,3),(3,5) case.
